title: Story of the Door
question: Today, can Mr. Utterson learn the name of the man who holds the key to that door?
light: hard grey light from the left, ink-black shadows
palette: soot black, bone white, gaslight amber, oxblood red

door_day.described: A narrow London by-street seen from its far pavement. Across the wet black cobbles a sinister two-storey block thrusts its gable forward: the upper storey is one flat forehead of discoloured, damp-stained grey plaster; the lower storey holds a single low door, blistered and distained, its brown paint peeling in scabs, set in a shallow recess above two worn stone steps. Bright shop fronts with freshly painted shutters and polished brass plates flank the block on both sides. A cold iron gas lamp stands at the kerb on the right. Grey Sunday daylight falls from the left down the length of the street, throwing the door's recess into deep black shadow.
door_day.landmark: the blistered brown door in its recess
door_day.landmark_size: a quarter of the frame's height
door_day.route: along the near pavement from the LEFT corner to the spot facing the door
door_day.geometry: In the establishing wide the grey plaster block fills the CENTRE half of the frame from the TOP edge down to the door lintel; the blistered door stands at the CENTRE of the lower third, a quarter of the frame's height, its two stone steps at the BOTTOM third. The shop fronts take the LEFT edge and the RIGHT edge, each a fifth of the frame's width. The gas lamp rises at the RIGHT third, half the frame's height. The cobbled roadway fills the BOTTOM edge between the near pavement and the door.
door_day.ambience: church bells far off, sparrows on the gutters, one cab's wheels on cobbles
door_day.place_state: black match-scorch streaks on the lower door panels, knife nicks on the mouldings, Sunday shutters closed on the shop fronts

night_cross_street.described: A London crossroads at three o'clock of a black winter morning. A soot-dark brick corner stands at the meeting of two streets, its shuttered windows dark, an iron gas lamp bracketed to the brick of the corner. Wet cobbles and frosted flagstones fill the crossing in front of it. The eastward street leads off to the LEFT under its own lamps; the cross street comes in from the RIGHT between dark terraces. The corner gas lamp lights the crossing from the left, throwing long ink-black shadows toward the RIGHT.
night_cross_street.landmark: the iron gas lamp on the corner
night_cross_street.landmark_size: a fifth of the frame's height
night_cross_street.route: along the eastward pavement from the LEFT edge to the corner
night_cross_street.geometry: In the establishing wide the brick corner stands at the CENTRE, a third of the frame's width, its gas lamp bracketed at the LEFT third, a fifth of the frame's height. The eastward pavement runs along the far side from the LEFT edge to the corner; the cross street opens at the RIGHT edge. The crossing of frosted cobbles fills the BOTTOM third, and the black night sky is a band along the TOP edge.
night_cross_street.ambience: a winter wind along the lamplit street, hissing gas jets, a dog barking far off
night_cross_street.place_state: black winter night, frost on the flagstones, every window dark, every gas lamp lit

night_door.described: The same narrow by-street at four in the morning. The sinister two-storey block thrusts its gable forward, its upper storey one flat forehead of discoloured grey plaster, its lower storey a single low blistered door in a shallow recess above two worn stone steps. Wet black cobbles shine in the foreground. A cold iron gas lamp at the kerb on the right burns with a hissing yellow flame, its light falling from the right across the door and the steps and throwing the recess and the neighbouring shop fronts into deep black shadow. Frost glitters along the kerbstones.
night_door.landmark: the lit iron gas lamp at the kerb
night_door.route: from the gas lamp at the kerb across the cobbles and up the two steps to the door
night_door.geometry: In the establishing wide the plaster block fills the CENTRE half of the frame from the TOP edge to the door lintel; the blistered door stands at the CENTRE of the lower third, a quarter of the frame's height, its steps at the BOTTOM third. The lit gas lamp rises at the RIGHT third, half the frame's height, its yellow pool spreading across the cobbles at the BOTTOM edge. Shadowed shop fronts take the LEFT edge, a fifth of the frame's width.
night_door.ambience: a hissing gas lamp, voices muttering off, a child sobbing far off
night_door.place_state: winter night at four in the morning, the kerb gas lamp lit, frost on the kerbstones

pavement_day.described: The flagstone pavement beside the entry of the court, at the foot of the sinister block. The blistered brown door stands in its shallow recess at the left, above two worn stone steps, its panels streaked with black match-scorch marks. The arched entry of the court opens beside it, a passage of soot-stained brick. Beyond, the by-street runs on with freshly painted shop shutters and polished brass plates. Grey Sunday daylight falls from the right along the pavement, throwing the recess and the court passage into deep black shadow.
pavement_day.landmark: the blistered door in its recess
pavement_day.route: from the door along the flagstones to the shop fronts at the RIGHT edge
pavement_day.geometry: In the establishing wide the blistered door and its recess fill the LEFT third of the frame, half the frame's height, the steps at the BOTTOM edge. The arched mouth of the court passage stands at the CENTRE, a third of the frame's height, black within. The pavement flagstones run from the BOTTOM LEFT corner toward the RIGHT edge, where the shop fronts with their painted shutters recede to a quarter of the frame's height.
pavement_day.ambience: pigeons on the gutters, distant cab wheels, a shop shutter rattling in the wind
pavement_day.place_state: Sunday daylight, black match-scorch streaks on the door panels, the brass keyhole polished bright

sunday_street.described: A bright by-street in a busy London quarter on a Sunday. Shop fronts line both pavements with freshly painted green and cream shutters, well-polished brass plates and door handles, and clean swept flagstones. Iron railings and lamp posts stand at even intervals along the kerbs. At the far end the street opens onto a dingy row of soot-black houses under a grey sky. Pale Sunday daylight falls from the left over the rooftops, gleaming on the brasses and laying sharp black shadows of the lamp posts across the cobbles toward the right.

sunday_street.landmark_size: a fifth of the frame's height
sunday_street.route: along the left-hand pavement from the near lamp post to the far end of the street
sunday_street.geometry: In the establishing wide the cobbled roadway leads from the BOTTOM edge to the CENTRE, narrowing to the dingy houses at the far end, a fifth of the frame's height. The shop fronts take the LEFT edge and the RIGHT edge, each a third of the frame's width, their brass plates glinting. A lamp post rises at the LEFT third, half the frame's height. The grey sky is a band along the TOP edge above the rooftops.

sunday_street.place_state: Sunday morning, shutters closed on the shop fronts, the brasses freshly polished

shots.at_rest: THE FOCUS OF THE PICTURE IS the lawyer's long, gaunt, rugged, unsmiling face at the CENTRE, his head a third of the frame's height under his black bowler hat, his eyes lowered. The shop fronts with green and cream shutters run behind him across the LEFT half; a lamp post stands at the RIGHT edge.
shots.end: The lawyer's face at the CENTRE, turned toward the RIGHT, his hand flat on his chest at the BOTTOM edge.
source: it is because I know it already
your tale has gone home
shots.turn: a listener -> a man who already knew
shots.why: The lawyer confesses the name means something to him: the hook for the book.

shots.frame: Medium of Mr. Enfield (light-brown top hat, fashionable dark frock coat) and the lawyer (black bowler hat, lawyer's dark suit) before the blistered door as Mr. Enfield taps the door's lock with his cane
shots.motion: The camera tracks beside the lawyer across to the door's; Mr. Enfield lifts his cane and taps its brass ferrule twice on the lock; the lawyer watches the cane
shots.camera: On the pavement at chest height, three yards from the door, a 35mm lens; the grey daylight comes from the RIGHT.
shots.at_rest: THE FOCUS OF THE PICTURE IS Mr. Enfield at the CENTRE, his head a quarter of the frame's height, his cane raised toward the door; the lawyer stands at the RIGHT third, his head a quarter of the frame's height. The blistered door fills the LEFT third, its lock at the height of Mr. Enfield's hand.
shots.end: Mr. Enfield's cane ferrule on the door's lock at the LEFT third, the two men at the CENTRE and the RIGHT third looking at it.
source: The fellow had a key
I saw him use it not a week ago.
shots.turn: a story -> a key still in use
shots.why: Enfield is certain the man still has the key: the danger is current.

shots.frame: Medium close over the lawyer's near shoulder and the back of his black bowler hat onto Mr. Enfield (receding brown hair, light-brown top hat) beside the blistered door as he offers his hand
shots.motion: The camera holds a locked-off frame; Mr. Enfield lowers his eyes and shakes his head at himself; he lifts his open hand toward the lawyer
shots.camera: Over the lawyer's shoulder, a yard behind his LEFT side at shoulder height, a 50mm lens; the grey daylight comes from the RIGHT.
shots.at_rest: THE FOCUS OF THE PICTURE IS Mr. Enfield's frank, lively face at the CENTRE, his head a third of the frame's height, his eyes lowered. The lawyer's dark shoulder and the back of his black bowler hat fill the LEFT edge; the blistered door's black recess sits behind Mr. Enfield at the RIGHT third.
shots.end: Mr. Enfield at the CENTRE, his open hand stretched toward the lawyer's shoulder at the LEFT edge.
source: I am ashamed of my long tongue.
Let us make a bargain never to refer to this again.
shots.turn: a long tongue -> a bargain of silence
shots.why: Enfield, ashamed, asks for silence; the lawyer must decide.

shots.frame: Insert of the hand of the lawyer (black bowler hat, lawyer's dark suit) clasping the hand of Mr. Enfield (light-brown top hat, fashionable dark frock coat) before the blistered door
shots.motion: The camera pushes in a hand's breadth toward the clasped hands, across the whole shot; the lawyer's hand grips Mr. Enfield's hand; the two hands shake, firm and even
shots.camera: At the height of the hands, a yard from them, a 50mm lens; the grey daylight comes from the RIGHT.
shots.at_rest: THE FOCUS OF THE PICTURE IS two hands meeting at the CENTRE, the lawyer's bony hand in a dark sleeve from the LEFT edge and Mr. Enfield's hand in a frock-coat cuff from the RIGHT edge. Behind them the blistered door's brown panels fill the TOP half, the worn stone step across the BOTTOM third.
shots.end: The two hands clasped at the CENTRE before the door panels.
source: With all my heart
I shake hands on that, Richard.
shots.turn: a bargain asked -> a bargain sealed
shots.why: The silence is sealed by a handshake at the door itself.

shots.frame: Medium close of the lawyer (long, gaunt, rugged, unsmiling face, black bowler hat) beside the blistered door as his hand closes at his waistcoat and he looks up at the blind wall
shots.motion: The camera tilts up from the lawyer's hand at his waistcoat to his long, unsmiling face across the whole shot; the lawyer's eyes go to the door at the LEFT; his face tips up toward the blind plaster wall
shots.camera: On the pavement a yard from him at chest height, a 50mm lens; the grey daylight comes from the RIGHT.
shots.at_rest: THE FOCUS OF THE PICTURE IS the lawyer's hand closing at the buttons of his dark waistcoat at the BOTTOM third. His long, gaunt face sits above at the TOP third, his head a third of the frame's height under his black bowler hat; the blistered door's black recess fills the LEFT edge behind him.
shots.end: The lawyer's face at the CENTRE, turned up toward the LEFT edge where the grey plaster wall rises above the door.
shots.changed: his eyes go to the wall
source: Mr. Utterson sighed deeply but said never a word
shots.turn: a sealed bargain -> an unsettled man
shots.why: The lawyer's silence is not peace; he looks at the wall that hides the man.

shots.frame: Wide of the narrow by-street as the lawyer (black bowler hat, lawyer's dark suit) and Mr. Enfield (light-brown top hat, fashionable dark frock coat) walk away along the near pavement and a ragged tramp strikes a match on the panels of the blistered door
shots.motion: The camera rises above the near pavement across the whole shot, looking down over the by-street and the door; the two men walk on to the RIGHT at a normal walking pace; the tramp strikes a match on the scorched door panel and its flame flares
shots.camera: On the near pavement at head height, ten yards from the door, a 35mm lens; the grey daylight comes from the LEFT.
shots.at_rest: THE FOCUS OF THE PICTURE IS the blistered brown door at the CENTRE of the lower third, a quarter of the frame's height, in its black recess under the flat grey plaster forehead. A ragged tramp slouches in the recess at the door's LEFT side; the lawyer and Mr. Enfield walk side by side at the BOTTOM RIGHT third on the near pavement, each a fifth of the frame's height; the gas lamp rises at the RIGHT third.
shots.end: The by-street seen from above, the blistered door at the CENTRE with a match flame at its LEFT side, the two men small at the RIGHT edge on the near pavement.
source: Tramps slouched into the recess and struck matches on the panels
I shake hands on that, Richard.
shots.turn: two men walk on -> the door keeps its secret
shots.why: The button: the world's answer, the door used by tramps as if nothing happened.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: A blind door on a bright Sunday street. Through it comes a man who tramples children.

lines.speaker: richard_enfield
lines.text: Did you ever remark that door? It's connected with a very odd story.

lines.speaker: gabriel_john_utterson
lines.text: Indeed? And what was that?

lines.speaker: richard_enfield
lines.text: Three o'clock of a black winter morning, street after street lit up, empty as a church.

lines.speaker: richard_enfield
lines.text: Then I saw a little man stumping along eastward at a good walk.

lines.speaker: richard_enfield
lines.text: And a girl of eight or ten, running as hard as she was able.

lines.speaker: richard_enfield
lines.text: They ran into one another at the corner. He trampled calmly over her and left her screaming.

lines.speaker: richard_enfield
lines.text: It was hellish to see. I collared my gentleman, and he gave me one look, so ugly.

lines.speaker: richard_enfield
lines.text: Cool as Satan, he says: no gentleman but wishes to avoid a scene. Name your figure.

lines.speaker: richard_enfield
lines.text: We screwed him up to a hundred pounds. He whipped out a key, and went in.

lines.speaker: richard_enfield
lines.text: He brought out gold, and a cheque signed with a name I can't mention. It was genuine.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Enfield calls it Black Mail House. His rule: the queerer a thing looks, the less he asks.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: They walk on in silence. Then the lawyer seizes Enfield's arm and demands the trampler's name.

lines.speaker: richard_enfield
lines.text: It was a man of the name of Hyde.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Enfield cannot describe him: something detestable, a deformity he cannot place.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The lawyer walks on, weighing every word.

lines.speaker: gabriel_john_utterson
lines.text: I know the other party's name already, Richard. Your tale has gone home.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Enfield is certain: the fellow has the key still, and used it not a week ago.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Ashamed of his long tongue, Enfield asks a bargain: never to speak of this again.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The lawyer gives his hand on it, with all his heart.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Behind them, the blind door keeps its secret, as it has for a generation.
